newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ANDERSON GOAL PUTS MONACO IN SIGHT OF SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ANDERSON GOAL PUTS MONACO IN SIGHT OF SEMIFINALS.

text.p: French league leaders Monaco, dominating more and more as the match progressed, scored a deserved 1-0 win over Newcastle United in their UEFA Cup quarter-final first leg at St James' Park on Tuesday night.

The only goal of a closely-fought match came after 59 minutes when 19-year-old Thierry Henry scampered free on the right and carried the ball to the by-line before cutting it back to Brazilian striker "Sonny" Anderson who lashed a right-foot first-time shot past two Newcastle defenders and goalkeeper Shaka Hislop.
The victory means Monaco have won all four of their UEFA Cup ties away from home this season.

Newcastle, playing without their injured 23 million pound ($37 million) first team strike-force of Alan Shearer and Les Ferdinand as well as suspended Colombian forward Faustino Asprilla, had few clearcut scoring chances and were increasingly outplayed and outrun in midfield where Monaco's Ali Benarbia was outstanding.
Newcastle's best chance came 10 minutes before the end but Belgian defender Philippe Albert skied his shot after goalkeeper Fabien Barthez had made an acrobatic save from Keith Gillespie.

Martin Djetou, substitute Victor Ikpeba and Benarbia all went close with other efforts for Jean Tigana's side who must now be favourites to advance to the semifinals after the second leg in two weeks time.

They became only the second team ever to win a European tie at Newcastle in 19 matches since 1968 and are on course to become the third French club to beat an English side in European competition out of a total of 20 meetings.
